claims.text: The nanoscale platinum-group-metal catalyst has high activity, selectivity, and durability in ethanol oxidation.
Potential-induced dynamic surface restructuring governs the catalyst's activity, selectivity, and durability.
Potential-induced restructuring forms a thin, controlled oxide/hydroxide surface layer.
The oxide/hydroxide layer exposes under-coordinated active sites.
The under-coordinated sites optimize adsorption and oxidation of ethanol intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption facilitates efficient multi-electron and multi-proton transfer.
An anodic potential pre-treatment induces surface restructuring and formation of a thin oxide/hydroxide layer.
The oxide/hydroxide film modulates adsorption energies.
Modulation of adsorption energies prevents poisoning by reaction intermediates.
The proposed surface film enhances overall ethanol-oxidation performance.
Anodically pre-treated catalysts will have lower ethanol-oxidation onset potentials than untreated catalysts.
Anodically pre-treated catalysts will have higher electrochemical current densities than untreated catalysts.
Anodically pre-treated catalysts will show greater selectivity toward complete ethanol-oxidation products than untreated catalysts.
Anodically pre-treated catalysts will be more durable than untreated catalysts.
The mechanism applies only within a potential window permitting controlled oxide/hydroxide formation.
Potentials too low to initiate restructuring will not produce the predicted effects.
Potentials high enough to cause uncontrolled oxidation may eliminate the predicted effects.
